name: Somalex
description: Somalex is a GABAergic positive allosteric modulator with a selective serotonin reuptake component, calibrated to eliminate social anxiety, reduce threat-processing, and promote affiliative behavior without sedation or cognitive blunting. It's the drug that makes you the best version of yourself at a party — present, warm, articulate, and completely unbothered.
effects: Complete elimination of social anxiety and self-consciousness
Heightened verbal fluency and conversational ease
Increased charisma — users become more persuasive and more likable simultaneously
side_effects: Impaired threat assessment — users become poor judges of dangerous situations or people
Lowered inhibition around personal information disclosure
Mild anterograde amnesia at higher doses — the party you had but can't fully remember
Emotional blunting during comedown — several hours of flat affect
Regular use erodes baseline social confidence, increasing dependency
street_price: Φ22 per dose (Φ8 generic on Shelf)
cultural_context: Somalex is the most widely consumed recreational drug in GLMZ. It is legal, socially accepted, and aggressively normalized. Tier 2 workers take it before shift-end socials. Tier 4 executives take it before client dinners. Shelf residents take the generic knockoff before block gatherings. The joke is that GLMZ runs on Somalex and you're not wrong. What is less discussed is the impaired threat assessment — and who benefits from a population that socializes without suspicion.
story_hooks: A routine corporate social event ended with three attendees signing documents they have no memory of signing — someone was using Somalex's disclosure-lowering effect deliberately, and the documents transferred significant assets

The Shelf generic version of Somalex has been quietly reformulated by an unknown party to include a compound that makes users more receptive to a specific political frequency broadcast — mass behavioral modification through the most mundane drug in the city
A character realizes they've been taking Somalex daily for so long that they no longer know what their unmedicated social self is like — and they're afraid to find out
